item.text: {"errors":[{"what":"“TRH (pulsatile)” labels the hypothalamus-to-anterior-pituitary arrow.","why_wrong":"The ovarian axis uses pulsatile GnRH. TRH primarily regulates TSH and prolactin.","severity":"error"},{"what":"“ACTH” and “TSH” label the two anterior-pituitary-to-ovary arrows.","why_wrong":"The ovarian gonadotropins are LH and FSH. ACTH primarily targets the adrenal cortex, and TSH targets the thyroid.","severity":"error"},{"what":"The dotted inhibin feedback ends at the pituitary output labeled “ACTH,” while its text says “FSH only (−).”","why_wrong":"The arrow contradicts the label and caption. It should terminate on an output labeled FSH.","severity":"error"},{"what":"“LH surge and a smaller FSH surge” sits beside the dashed ovarian feedback arrows, but neither pituitary output shows a surge.","why_wrong":"The diagram names the surges without showing increased LH and FSH release toward the ovary, so the causal sequence is incomplete.","severity":"misleading"},{"what":"The labels and explanatory lines are very small, and most of the image below the figure is blank.","why_wrong":"The unused space makes the teaching content difficult to read at the supplied size.","severity":"cosmetic"}],"legibility":2,"teaches_caption":false,"overall":3,"verdict":"The feedback descriptions are largely sound, but the central hormone labels are wrong. Replace TRH with GnRH and ACTH/TSH with LH/FSH, align the inhibin bar with FSH, and show the surge on the pituitary outputs."}
